PullRequest.Title: Chat: unify Agent Host status pills across chat surfaces
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

This pull request brings Agent Host session status pills to editor and panel chat inputs and, more importantly, consolidates the Agents Window and editor/panel implementations onto the same reusable pill architecture.

The result is one shared composition and lifecycle path for Changes, Pull Requests, Issues, Artifacts, References, Browsers, Customizations, and Subagents. Each surface now supplies observable data and an allowed set of pill kinds; it no longer independently decides ordering, rendering, compact behavior, visibility, keyboard behavior, or dropdown mechanics.

## User experience

- Shows session status pills above the chat input for Agent Host-backed editor and panel chats.
- Keeps Local chat inputs pill-free. The editor/panel integration is intentionally Agent Host-specific.
- Offers these editor/panel pill kinds:
  - Changes
  - Pull Requests
  - Issues
  - Artifacts
  - References
  - Browsers
- Keeps Agents Window-only data such as Customizations and Subagents available in the Agents Window without exposing inappropriate worktree-specific UI in editor/panel chat.
- Uses the existing `chat.turnStatusPills` setting, which remains enabled by default.
- Preserves chat pet interaction by publishing the same rendered pill elements as horizontal pet platforms.
- Uses responsive compact behavior in smaller chat surfaces: pills remain expanded while they fit and collapse to icon-only presentation only when the row would overflow.

## Shared architecture

### One controller for both surfaces

`ChatInputPills` now owns the common row and widget lifecycle:

- setting enablement;
- per-kind user visibility;
- the visibility context menu and hidden-pill recovery state;
- row and widget creation;
- keyboard and focus restoration;
- chat pet element publication;
- visible/hidden lifecycle notifications.

Both the Agents Window and Agent Host editor/panel adapter instantiate this controller instead of maintaining separate toolbar implementations.

### One canonical pill composition

`StandardChatInputPillSources` is the canonical builder for the standard session pill set. It owns:

- pill ordering;
- component selection;
- Changes rendering and activation;
- Pull Request, Issue, Artifact, Reference, Browser, Customization, and Subagent section pills;
- shared per-kind labels, icons, summaries, and single-entry behavior.

The two surfaces only provide observable sections, callbacks, and the kinds they support. This prevents presentation drift such as the previously different Pull Request pill between the Agents Window and editor chat.

### Shared presentation helpers

- Common Pull Request state-to-icon and aggregate-priority logic moved into shared workbench code.
- Common session pill options moved into a shared options module.
- Live Pull Request presentation is resolved once through a reusable Sessions model, while polling remains centrally owned by the existing GitHub polling contribution.
- Provider-specific session and changeset resolution remains in Agent Host connection/provider policy rather than being reconstructed by the UI.

### Removed duplicate pill path

The old `SessionHeaderMeta` metadata-pill path is no longer needed after the input toolbar migration. This change removes:

- `SessionMetadataPills`;
- specialized Changes, Pull Request, and Issue header action view items;
- their action-view-item registrations;
- legacy component fixtures and tests that exercised the now-unreachable header implementation.

The commands themselves remain available for the shared pills and session context menus. This leaves a single active rendering architecture instead of two independently evolving implementations.

## Flicker and lifecycle improvements

The shared pill primitives were updated to avoid rebuilding UI for routine observable changes:

- Pill membership updates are incremental and preserve existing DOM nodes.
- Existing pill buttons and keyboard focus survive unrelated pill additions and removals.
- An open dropdown remains open when an unrelated pill changes.
- If the open pill itself disappears, focus moves to the nearest remaining pill, the empty configuration row, or the owning chat input.
- Open dropdown contents update in place when their observable sections change and close when the pill is no longer summarized.
- Stable section-pill descriptors prevent toolbar recreation while visible presentation is unchanged.
- Dropdown buttons update only the label, tooltip, icon, and accessibility state that actually changed.
- Responsive compact measurement caches intrinsic pill width instead of repeatedly measuring the viewport-sized row.
- The intrinsic-width cache is invalidated only when pill sizing changes.
- Agent Host change summaries retain the last authoritative files during transient changeset recomputation and clear only when a ready changeset is authoritatively empty.
- Change caches are isolated by connection authority and changeset URI.

These changes address the visible flashing during session startup, new pill discovery, changeset recomputation, and session completion.

## Agent Host and GitHub correctness

- Editor/panel pills resolve the backend session URI, scheme aliases, relative changeset templates, and configured default changeset kind through shared Agent Host connection policy.
- Cloud Sandbox aliases therefore resolve to the correct backend session and changeset channel.
- Browser pills include browsers owned by direct tool-origin subagent chats.
- Hiding the Browser pill allows matching website artifacts or references to appear in their corresponding pills instead of disappearing entirely.
- Pull Request state is applied only to the URL it describes; unrelated Pull Requests keep their own open/default state.
- Pull Request summary icons are derived from the per-entry icons using shared priority rules.
- Agents Window Pull Request pills retain live CI/review state and Agent Merge-aware blocker presentation.
- Combined failing-check and unresolved-review states are announced together.
- Cached draft, merged, and closed Pull Request icons retain matching accessible state before live details arrive.
- Pull Request polling is not duplicated by the presentation layer.
- Issue refresh/polling only runs while the Issue pill feature is enabled and visible.

## Accessibility

- The row and pills keep consistent toolbar, button, listbox, and popup semantics.
- The empty hidden-pill recovery row is keyboard accessible and exposes `aria-haspopup="menu"`.
- Inline single-entry and single-resource pills expose both their actionable label and their status/location description.
- Focus is preserved across incremental updates and safely restored when a focused or expanded pill disappears.
- Auxiliary-window rendering uses the correct DOM realm and target-window observers.
- Sessions accessibility help now describes status pills above the chat input rather than the removed session-header controls.

## Validation

Validated after rebasing onto the latest `main`:

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- ESLint across all TypeScript files changed by the PR
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- 197 focused workbench, Sessions, Agent Host changeset, GitHub, accessibility, and pill unit tests
- forced `npm run build-fast -- --force`
- Component Explorer checks for:
  - the shared `3 Pull Requests` summary/dropdown presentation;
  - the `1 File +12 -5` Changes presentation;
  - responsive expanded/compact behavior.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added auto-compact resize callback and geometry reads are directly traced: ResizeObserver calls layout on container changes, and line 202 unconditionally re-enters the measurement block whenever the row is expanded. Mutations and observed child resizes already invalidate the cache, so the repeated measurement during a pure width drag is not needed; exact frame cost varies with DOM/theme complexity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous DOM geometry/style resolution for the pill toolbar subtree
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost repeats for each ResizeObserver delivery during a panel/editor drag and grows with the rendered pill toolbar subtree.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated forced layout on the resize critical path can increase resize latency and drop frames.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The previous session toolbar resize observer only rescanned the scrollable node, and editor/panel chat had no responsive pill row; it did not remove compact styling and remeasure intrinsic pill width on every expanded-state resize.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Auto-compact rows now call layout for each observed resize, and the added `|| !...compact` condition recomputes expanded width even when `_expandedContentWidth` is already cached and only available width changed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 202 explicitly bypasses the new `_expandedContentWidth` cache whenever the row is expanded, placing intrinsic subtree measurement on every resize callback.
Findings.Title: Reuse the intrinsic-width cache while the row is expanded
Findings.Impact: Dragging the chat panel boundary or resizing a chat editor while pills fit keeps the row expanded, so every resize delivery reads `getBoundingClientRect`, removes compact styling, and reads offsets/widths before paint, causing avoidable resize jank.
Findings.Evidence: `ChatPillsRow` observes `content` and its pill element and calls `layout()` from the ResizeObserver. In `layout`, line 201 reads the viewport width; line 202 enters the intrinsic-width block whenever the row is not compact, and lines 205-206 read `offsetLeft`/`offsetWidth`. `_expandedContentWidth` is already invalidated by MutationObserver and non-content ResizeObserver entries, proving pure container-width changes can reuse it.
Findings.Recommendation: Measure intrinsic width only when `_expandedContentWidth` is undefined; keep the existing mutation and child-resize invalidation paths for real sizing changes.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The observable call path is explicit: the Changes source's `hasData` reads `changeStats`, which reads `changes`, so the mapping runs as part of normal pill presentation rather than only when the user opens Changes. Each helper call parses and canonicalizes before/after/content URIs and wraps resources. The exact largest changeset size is uncertain, affecting severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Parsed/wrapped URI objects and per-file diff objects, plus repeated collection scans
Findings.PerformanceScaling: CPU and allocation grow linearly with the number of files in the session-wide changeset and recur on each authoritative changeset update for each open Agent Host chat surface.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Large changesets add synchronous CPU and GC pressure to session-state delivery and pill rendering, increasing chat UI latency.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Editor and panel chat did not create this session-wide Changes pill or materialize changeset files. The Agents Window summary path aggregated counts directly from session changes/summary without creating editor diff resources for every file.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new Agent Host input adapter maps every changeset file through `agentHostChangesetFileToEntryDiff` before computing three scalar pill counts, even when the Changes pill is never activated.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 294 eagerly invokes the URI-heavy diff conversion for every file in the newly subscribed session changeset on the pill's observed rendering path.
Findings.Title: Defer materializing every changeset diff until activation
Findings.Impact: Opening or updating an Agent Host session with hundreds or thousands of changed files synchronously parses up to four URIs per file, creates wrapped Agent Host URIs and diff objects, then scans the result again for additions/deletions; this can visibly delay pill/chat updates and create GC churn.
Findings.Evidence: Line 294 maps the full `ChangesetState.files` array. `agentHostChangesetFileToEntryDiff` calls `normalizeFileEdit`, which parses before/after and content URIs and canonicalizes them, then creates wrapped original/modified/snapshot URIs and a diff object. `changeStats` immediately consumes that allocated array only to read length and reduce additions/deletions twice; the array is otherwise needed only by the Changes click handler.
Findings.Recommendation: Derive files/additions/deletions directly from the raw changeset entries for presentation, retain the raw files, and convert them to `IEditSessionEntryDiff` only inside the Changes activation path (or memoize that conversion on first activation).

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or update an Agent Host-backed editor/panel chat and render session status pills
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The widget resolves the session, acquires session and default-changeset subscriptions, derives pill sources, and synchronously computes Changes stats before the status row can settle. Opening the multi-diff editor is user-triggered and off the initial rendering path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to Agent Host Session state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One subscription per live Agent Host chat widget; zero for Local chat or while pills are disabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Editor/panel chats had no Agent Host input-pill adapter and did not add this session-state subscription for status pills.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session metadata and the changeset catalogue must arrive before these pills can be composed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to the resolved default Agent Host Changeset state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one selected changeset subscription per live Agent Host chat widget, replaced when resolution/target changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Editor/panel chats did not subscribe to a session-wide changeset for input pills.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The Changes pill waits on this state and then synchronously processes its full file array.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve Agent Host file/content resources when the user opens Changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One multi-diff editor open containing one resource tuple per effective changed file, only on explicit activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no editor/panel session-wide Changes pill activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the pill-rendering critical path; filesystem/content reads occur when the editor resolves the selected diffs.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of files in the selected session-wide changeset; effective cardinality is the full raw file array for each authoritative update, with no grouping before URI conversion.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One session subscription and at most one changeset subscription per live chat widget; multiple open editor/panel widgets own independent observable/reference lifecycles, while each widget serially derives its state.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolution and changeset target use equality-aware derived observables; transient changeset recomputation retains the last matching ready files. The new code nevertheless eagerly recreates all editor diff/URI objects whenever an authoritative file array changes, with no lazy activation cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the observed Changes `hasData` path reads stats, which reads the eagerly mapped diff array, and the conversion helper visibly parses/canonicalizes/wraps multiple URIs per file.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical changesets may be small, but repository-wide agent changes can realistically contain hundreds or thousands of files; exact URI-conversion and GC duration depends on file count and host URI shapes.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager-work regression: editor/panel pill rendering materializes every diff resource merely to display scalar counts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize a chat panel/editor with responsive status pills visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each ResizeObserver delivery synchronously runs `ChatPillsRow.layout`; geometry reads and scrollable scanning happen before the resize frame can paint.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Resize event frequency during a drag, multiplied by rendered pill-row DOM complexity; effective pill cardinality is up to the six editor/panel kinds or eight Agents Window kinds.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser resize deliveries are serialized on the UI thread; there is no debounce or frame coalescing in the added row logic.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An intrinsic expanded-width cache exists and is invalidated on descendant mutation or observed child resize, but the expanded-state condition bypasses it on every pure container resize.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ResizeObserver calls `layout`, and the added expanded-state branch re-reads offsets/widths despite a populated cache.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Absolute layout cost depends on browser, theme, and pill DOM size, but continuous panel dragging supplies frame-rate-frequency triggers.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable synchronous-layout regression: cached intrinsic width is remeasured on every expanded-state resize.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render Agents Window Pull Request and Issue pills with live GitHub state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session observables compose pill entries immediately from cached model state; GitHub refresh/poll results arrive asynchronously and are not required for initial row rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh and poll referenced GitHub issues
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared model refresh/poll stream per unique issue while the feature and Issue pill are visible; hidden/disabled issues do not refresh or poll.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed Issue action view item already refreshed and polled each referenced issue whenever rendered; the new placement narrows activity to enabled and visible pills.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous enrichment; initial pills can render unresolved/default state without waiting.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh and poll Pull Request, CI, and review-thread models
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Shared per unique Pull Request identity, with CI/review streams only for open non-draft Pull Requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Central GitHub polling already owned these calls; the new presentation model explicitly does not refresh or start polling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous live-status enrichment and off the initial pill composition critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective unique Pull Request and Issue references in the active/visible session after shared reference collections; normally small, but network cardinality is one model refresh/poll stream per unique reference.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ReferenceCollection shares models by GitHub identity. Issue polling runs only while pills are enabled and the Issue kind is visible; Pull Request polling remains centrally owned by the existing polling contribution.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Issue models debounce refresh for 60 seconds, retain up to 100 disposed snapshots, use ETags, and share references. Pull Request presentation acquires existing shared models and does not start duplicate polling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call ownership and model-reference/polling behavior are explicit in the changed toolbar and existing GitHub contribution/model code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions can reference multiple GitHub objects, but shared identity models, visibility gating, ETags, and long issue polling intervals bound repeated traffic.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: issue work is more tightly gated and Pull Request presentation does not duplicate network polling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render completed-turn file-change summaries and open changed-file diffs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing Agent Host response/changeset observables derive per-turn diffs; the diff list and scalar summary update synchronously, while editor/file-content resolution occurs only after user activation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Consume Agent Host session/chat/changeset subscription state for response changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing subscription set per observed request/session, with response edits grouped by URI before rendering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider already subscribed to the same Agent Host state components and mapped changeset/response files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provides authoritative summary data; this diff changes transformation/empty semantics but does not add a new subscription boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve original and snapshot resources in diff or multi-diff editors
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One editor open with one resource tuple per effective diff, only after explicit user activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Changed-file activation already opened diff resources; this refactor selects snapshot/create/delete sides more precisely.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of tool-call file edits or changeset files in one turn, deduplicated by modified URI for response edits.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: State updates are processed serially through observables; editor opening is a single multi-diff request containing all selected resources.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-request observables remain bounded by the existing 1000-entry request cache; transient empty values retain prior diffs, while the new sentinel allows authoritative empty results to clear them.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed code preserves the same subscription/mapping path and only adjusts resource selection and authoritative-empty handling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large turns can contain many edits, but grouping and the existing request cache bound effective retained cardinality; no new multiplicative boundary was introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a Local (non-Agent Host) chat in the editor or panel
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The adapter is constructed with the widget, but session resolution returns undefined; source derivations produce no pills and do not acquire Agent Host state subscriptions.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of concurrently instantiated local chat widgets and globally known browser views.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No Agent Host IPC or GitHub network work is started. Each widget owns a browser-view listener set and refresh signal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolution equality prevents downstream recomputation for unchanged undefined resolution; hidden row data remains empty.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for absence of Agent Host/GitHub boundaries; low magnitude for the remaining listener bookkeeping.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The adapter does attach browser-view listeners even for Local chats, but realistic widget/browser counts and callback work are too small to establish a concrete user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression for Local chats.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 75 changed files. Submitted two medium-confidence-impact findings: repeated synchronous intrinsic-width measurement during responsive resizing, and eager per-file URI/diff materialization for Agent Host Changes stats. GitHub polling, response-change boundaries, cache lifecycles, cleanup, and Local-chat gating did not introduce additional reportable regressions.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
